valuationInputs.name: Beta
valuationInputs.reason: 8 steps, 21 Nov 2026. (1) Business: one business, PVC compound for cables (plus a small recycling subsidiary, ACL Polymers), so one sector beta: specialty chemicals. (2) Damodaran's emerging-markets dataset (betaEmerg) couldn't be reached in this run (pages.stern.nyu.edu blocked); used his global Chemical (Specialty) unlevered beta for January 2026, 0.98 (1.04 corrected for cash, 952 firms), via web search. (3) Relevered at net debt to market value: net debt at 30 Sep 2026 is Rs 0.21bn of borrowings less Rs 0.01bn cash against a market value of Rs 6.6bn (D/E 0.03), and the Rs 2.5bn of unit trusts and deposits more than cover it, so D/E is taken as 0: 0.98. (4) Local 5-year betas: only one found (StockAnalysis 0.20); the share is thinly traded (33.9% float, 3,508 public holders), so local betas are ignored. (5) Higher of (3) and (4): 0.98. (6) Within 0.3–2. (7)-(8) Put into the calculator and shown as the Required return tile. Refresh in January 2027 with the emerging-markets figure.

valuationInputs.name: Cost of equity
valuationInputs.reason: From scripts/reinvestment.py (21 Nov 2026): 8.24% + 0.98 × (4.2% + 6.08%) = 18.3%, ±1.5 points. Replaces the hand-set 18% / 16.5% / 15% of 11 Nov.

valuationInputs.name: WACC
valuationInputs.reason: From scripts/reinvestment.py (21 Nov 2026): net debt Rs 0.21bn (Rs 0.22bn short-term loans and overdraft less Rs 0.01bn cash, 30 Sep 2026) against market value Rs 6.58bn, debt weight 3.0%. Cost of debt is the 12.24% bond yield because there were no borrowings at March 2025 or 2026 (interest paid Rs 0.98mn).

valuationInputs.name: Growth check
valuationInputs.value: Assumed 3% / 5.5% / 6.5%; supported 4.8% (reinvestment rate 24.4% × return on capital 19.9%, FY 2026). All within 2 pts.
valuationInputs.reason: From scripts/reinvestment.py on FY 2026. Return on capital is on total equity, which includes Rs 2.7bn of unit trusts and deposits; on the PVC business alone it is nearer 28%. Revenue grew 17% in FY 2026 and 16% in H1 FY2027, mostly volume for ACL Cables and Kelani Cables.

valuationInputs.name: Growth
valuationInputs.value: Bear 3% then 4% / Base 5.5% then 4.5% / Bull 6.5% then 5%
valuationInputs.reason: Five years, then long-run, below the 12.24% bond yield and WACC. Revenue grew 3% a year from FY 2022 (Rs 2.96bn) to FY 2026 (Rs 2.85bn) including the 2023–24 slump; sales depend on the parent's cable volumes.

valuationInputs.name: Return on new capital
valuationInputs.reason: PVC business after-tax profit Rs 0.66bn (twelve months to Sep 2026) over operating capital about Rs 2.4bn (equity 4.70 − unit trusts 1.45 − deposits 0.96 − FVOCI shares 0.12 + net debt 0.21, 30 Sep 2026) ≈ 28%; new capital is mostly stock and receivables, so a lower range.

valuationInputs.name: After-tax operating profit (start)
valuationInputs.value: Bear quarter × 4 / Base FY 2026 / Bull twelve months to Sep 2026 (calculated)
valuationInputs.reason: Business profit = gross profit less administrative costs (unit-trust gains and dividends excluded, because the annual report puts them in operating profit and the interims in finance income), after the FY 2026 tax rate of 28.1%: bear the September 2026 quarter × 4 (gross margin 24.9%), base FY 2026 (31%), bull the twelve months to September 2026.

valuationInputs.name: Cash after maintenance capex (start)
valuationInputs.value: After-tax business profit + depreciation − maintenance capex (calculated)
valuationInputs.reason: Not the calculator's FY 2026 operating cash (Rs 0.50bn) or the twelve-month figure (−Rs 0.52bn), which swing with stock and receivables owed by the parent; the DCF charges working capital as reinvestment instead. Maintenance capex from the calculator range (Rs 27mn / 16mn / 16mn).

valuationInputs.name: Maintenance capex basis
valuationInputs.reason: No company split. Capex booked Rs 53mn in FY 2026 (Rs 26.5mn of it a motor vehicle, Rs 25.8mn machinery and equipment) against depreciation Rs 16mn; Rs 1.3mn in FY 2025. No growth project named, no capital commitments.

valuationInputs.name: Treasury investments (add-on)
valuationInputs.value: Unit trusts + short-term deposits + FVOCI shares at book, per share (Rs 59.86 at 30 Sep 2026)
valuationInputs.reason: Rs 1,445mn unit trusts + Rs 956mn deposits + Rs 120mn listed shares (Interim to 30 Sep 2026, p. 4) ÷ 42.125mn shares; the 1000 converts Rs bn to Rs a share. Added to the DCF of the PVC business in every case: liquid, carried at market or cost plus interest.

valuationInputs.name: Long-run ROE
valuationInputs.reason: ROE (profit over average equity, Decade at a Glance) 37% FY 2022, 25% FY 2023, 15% FY 2024, 13% FY 2025, 20% FY 2026, 21% twelve months to Sep 2026; equity is 54% cash and investments, which caps ROE.

valuationInputs.name: Long-term growth
valuationInputs.reason: Same in every method; below the 12.24% bond yield. Was 6% / 6.5% / 7%.

valuationInputs.name: EPS to March 2027 × P/E
valuationInputs.reason: H1 EPS Rs 10.72; second half Rs 6.98 / 8.48 / 10.48 (last year Rs 10.57, Sep 2026 quarter Rs 3.73 as margin fell to 24.9%). Base 9.8% below the Rs 21.29 run-rate. P/E justified at the cost of equity: (1 − g ÷ ROE) ÷ (cost of equity − g).

valuationInputs.name: Residual income start
valuationInputs.value: ROE 20.7% (twelve months to Sep 2026, calculated); payout 20%
valuationInputs.reason: Payout: Rs 3.75 for 2025/26 against EPS Rs 18.94.

valuationInputs.name: Methods used
valuationInputs.value: DCF of the PVC business + treasury investments, P/E, justified P/B, residual income
valuationInputs.reason: Dividend model left out: payout about 20%, so its value would rest on the payout assumed after year five. Weighted equally.

openQuestions: Q3 results (to December 2026, due by mid-February): does the gross margin recover from 25%?
Do stock and receivables (up Rs 663mn in H1) come back down, and is the Rs 200mn loan repaid?
Any change in how much ACL Cables and Kelani Cables buy, or at what price.
How much of profit comes from unit-trust and exchange gains.
